findings.on_main: fails the same way (6 of 20 sampled, reply exactly 65,536 bytes)
findings.verdict: existing limit on main, not a regression
findings.root_cause: scripts/gtm-brain-entities/entities.mjs prints --relations with console.log and then calls process.exit(0). The MCP server reads the script through a pipe (server.mjs run, execFile), and on macOS the exit drops everything after the first 64 KiB of pipe buffer. Run with stdout to a file the script writes all 179 KiB and nothing is missing. The lines in entities.mjs are unchanged between main and the release. It is the same defect lane A fixed for compile --facts (the finish helper in compile.mjs); entities.mjs was not in that lane.
findings.action: marked known_gap in e2e.mjs (PIPE_CUT) with the byte count in the note. Not fixed here: the instruction for an existing limit was to mark it. The fix is the compile.mjs finish helper (await the stdout write, then exit), plus a decision on how much of a 180 KiB list a model should get.

findings.on_main: fails the same way (9 of 10, reply exactly 65,536 bytes)
findings.verdict: existing limit on main, not a regression
findings.root_cause: The same pipe cut: entities.mjs --customers prints JSON (339 KiB for the medium brain) with console.log, then process.exit(0). The reply the model gets is the first 64 KiB of a JSON document, so it is also invalid JSON.

findings.on_release: passes on a quiet machine: the e2e run twice, and a separate probe (one batch of three over MCP, each note queried at once) four times, every note found
findings.verdict: not reproduced; the earlier failure came from the overloaded machine, the exact path is not proven
findings.root_cause: Not a lost write: remember.mjs --batch writes the three notes before it prints, and the earlier run reported no remember error. The read after it goes through the memory index, which refuses to answer rather than return partial rows when its refresh does not finish (sync budget 20 s, reader limit 60 s including queue wait, 'refresh is in progress'). The check counted any reply without rows as missing, so a refused or late read under load average 20 to 120 looked like a missing note. The earlier reply text was not kept (that run's debug file is empty: the harness crashed in cleanup).
findings.action: harness: on a miss the check now records whether the read failed or came back empty and whether the note is there 2 s later. Pass still needs all three at once.

findings.root_cause: runChecks killed the server and removed the scratch brain in the same tick; a child of the server was still writing into work/, rmSync threw ENOTEMPTY and the whole run's results were lost (first main medium run here, and the empty medium-debug.json of the earlier run).
findings.action: e2e.mjs waits for the server to exit and treats cleanup as best effort.

unverified: messy, large, the suite and the live cases: in progress
